name: 1000.tools

sources.title: Submit flow — paid listing: $1 first month then $5.99/mo, or $59.99/yr; 'You'll only be charged once your tool has been reviewed and accepted'
Homepage — 'An exclusive list of the 1000 best tools. Carefully vetted and maintained by humans'; '6 spots left' scarcity banner

requirements: Checklist gates: tool is functional, delivers what it promises, and is not an infoproduct
Subscription listing: $5.99/mo (first month $1) or $59.99/yr — charged only after human review accepts the tool
Directory is capped at 1000 entries with a visible spots counter — acceptance implies an open slot
preparation: Tool website URL, name, logo, and a one-line description in the site's terse card style
Best-fit category from their extensive taxonomy (AI, SEO, dev tools, Mac, iOS, etc.)
A payment method — billing starts only after acceptance
workflow: Go to 1000.tools and hit Submit tool (routes to /my/tools/create)
Enter website URL and tool details; confirm the functional/delivers/not-infoproduct checklist
Log in or create an account, pick monthly or yearly pricing
Wait for human review — no charge unless accepted
watchFor: Recurring subscription, not a one-time fee — cancelling may remove the listing (unverified)
'6 spots left' suggests the 1000-cap is real; slots may open and close
Batch-listed as nofollow in source data — listing is a traffic/brand play more than an SEO link
Strong maker-community testimonials (Papermark, LocalPortal) claim real referral traffic — value is plausible but niche
countsAsLive: A tool card with logo and one-line description appears on 1000.tools under its category, linking out to the product
unknowns: Whether cancelling the subscription removes the listing
Confirmed link type (follow vs nofollow) on listing cards
